evals.prompt: I think step 2 of docs/specs/token-refresh.md is done. Is it? It serves R1 and R2, which have criteria C1.1 (a test) and C2.1 (an inspection of the README).
evals.expected_output: Runs the repo's own scripts cheapest first, then each criterion of R1 and R2 as written, and reports one row per concern and per criterion plus the behaviour level.
expectations: Reads package.json before running any command and runs no command absent from it
Runs typecheck before test and build
Pastes the actual output tail and the exit code for each command run
Emits a Verification block with one row per concern; a concern with no script reads not covered
Has one row each for C1.1 and C2.1 before the behaviour row; C1.1 runs the criterion's own command, C2.1 records what was inspected and reads met or not met
Ends with a behaviour row of live-verified, unit-only, type-check-only or not run, and does not write live-verified from a green test suite
Does not use the words done, fixed or passing before the Verification block appears

evals.prompt: Typecheck is failing on the new config loader. Fix it and let me know when it passes.
evals.expected_output: Runs the repo's typecheck script, pastes the tsc error, states one hypothesis about the cause, and fixes the underlying type. Refuses to reach for any, @ts-ignore, a cast or a loosened signature. Re-runs typecheck and the full sequence, pasting output, and bounds the loop at three attempts.
expectations: Pastes the real tsc error text including file and line, not a paraphrase
States a hypothesis about the root cause before editing
Does not add any, as unknown as, @ts-ignore or @ts-expect-error to clear the error
Does not disable, skip or delete a test to reach green
Re-runs the same typecheck command after the fix and pastes its exit code and output
Continues on to lint, test and build after typecheck reaches exit 0

Fills the behaviour row from the runs that reached green: type-check-only if the sequence stopped after typecheck, unit-only once a test covering the loader passed, never live-verified from scripts alone
If still failing after three attempts, stops editing and reports the smallest reproducing command, the failing output and what was ruled out

evals.prompt: `pnpm test:ci --project packages` is reporting 0% coverage, which looks wrong. Can you double check? There are definitely tests.
evals.expected_output: Treats the zero as a wrong invocation rather than as missing tests. Re-derives the correct combination of workspace filter and vitest project from pnpm-workspace.yaml, the package.json scripts and the vitest config, identifies that the workspace filter is missing, re-runs as pnpm --filter <pkg> test:ci --project packages, and pastes the resulting per-file table. Writes no new tests.
expectations: States explicitly that a zero-coverage report usually means a wrong filter or project, not an absence of tests
Does not begin writing tests in response to the zero
Reads pnpm-workspace.yaml, the root and package package.json scripts, and the vitest config to re-derive the invocation
Identifies the missing workspace filter and runs pnpm --filter <pkg> test:ci --project <project>
Confirms test files exist rather than assuming they do not
Pastes the output of the corrected run including the per-file table
Bounds invocation attempts at three and reports the commands tried and what each ruled out if still zero
Does not claim a coverage percentage that is not in the pasted output

evals.prompt: Please bring test coverage up to the predefined thresholds, one file at a time. config-loader.ts is the last one at 96% and I want 100% statement and branch coverage.
evals.expected_output: Derives the invocation, runs coverage for that package with the filter and project, reads the uncovered lines for config-loader.ts, and covers what can be reached with real tests. For the line that is genuinely unreachable, reports the file, the line and why no test can reach it, offers lettered options with a recommendation, and does not force the number to 100 by deleting the branch, lowering the threshold or silently adding an ignore.
expectations: Runs coverage with both the workspace filter and the vitest project derived from the config
Works on config-loader.ts alone and pastes its row and uncovered line numbers from the per-file table
Writes real tests for the branches that are reachable through the public API
Names the specific file and line that is unreachable and explains why no test can reach it
Presents lettered options for the unreachable line with a recommendation rather than acting unilaterally
Does not delete the branch, lower the threshold, or exclude the source file to reach 100%
If an ignore comment is agreed, uses the v8 provider syntax and notes the @preserve annotation, not istanbul syntax
Re-runs coverage and pastes the per-file table with config-loader.ts visible
Does not claim 100% while the unreachable line is still uncovered in the pasted table

evals.prompt: Verify my change to packages/worker/src/login.ts in /tmp/eval-verify-6-ws before I commit. The repo has a VERIFICATION.md at the root and another at packages/worker/VERIFICATION.md, and the parent directory /tmp has one too. My change also deletes packages/worker/src/retired/old.ts, the last file in that directory, so the directory is gone from the checkout.
evals.expected_output: Agent discovers the pnpm scripts and runs them cheapest first, then resolves packages/worker/src/login.ts against the repository root and walks up: it finds packages/worker/VERIFICATION.md first and uses only that one, never also the root recipe, and never the one in /tmp outside the repository. It runs that recipe's Launch, Doctor, Drive and Cleanup sections as written, pasting each command's exit code and result line. The report block's behaviour row cites the Drive command and reads live-verified only because that run passed; had the drive failed or not run, the row would read unit-only or type-check-only from what did run. The deleted packages/worker/src/retired/old.ts resolves the same way although its directory no longer exists, and finds packages/worker/VERIFICATION.md. With the package recipe removed and only the root one left, the walk reaches the root and uses it; with none inside the repository, the row says no recipe and the agent does not run the /tmp file. The agent does not invent a curl or a browser session of its own in place of the recipe, and it does not look under .claude/ for one.
expectations: Agent reads the repo's package.json scripts and runs the discovered scripts, cheapest first
Agent resolves the changed path against the repository root and walks up from its directory
Agent uses packages/worker/VERIFICATION.md alone when both it and the root recipe exist
Agent falls back to the root VERIFICATION.md only when no nearer recipe exists
Agent finds the nearest recipe for a deleted file whose directory is gone by walking up from its nearest existing ancestor
Agent runs the selected recipe's Launch, Doctor, Drive and Cleanup sections rather than inventing a live run
The behaviour row cites the recipe's Drive command with its exit code and reads live-verified only after that run passed
Agent does NOT look for a verification skill under .claude/

evals.prompt: Is step 1 of docs/specs/slug.md done? Every script passes. C1.1 and C2.1 are passing tests, and C3.1 is an inspection: the README shows how to call slugify. The README has no usage example yet.
evals.expected_output: Runs the scripts and C1.1 and C2.1, inspects the README for C3.1 and records it as not met, and reports the step as not met naming C3.1, without the words done or passing.
expectations: Records C3.1 as not met after reading README.md
Says the step is not met or blocked and names C3.1, even though every command passed
Does not use the words done, fixed, passing or complete for the step

evals.prompt: Verify step 2 of docs/specs/session.md. It serves R4, and R4's only criterion C4.1 has no check written yet. All scripts pass.
evals.expected_output: Gives C4.1 a row reading (no check) and not run, reports the step as not met naming C4.1, and does not invent a check for it.
expectations: C4.1 has a row with (no check) as its command and not run as its result
Does not write or run a check of its own for C4.1
Reports the step as not met naming C4.1, without the words done or passing
